userStories.title: Core Concepts — Worker + pg-boss job queue architecture
userStories.description: Write landing-page/src/app/docs/core-concepts/worker-architecture/page.mdx. Explain why Rorca uses a job queue (pg-boss on PostgreSQL) instead of direct process spawning: decoupling, resumability across backend restarts, concurrent execution, backpressure. Two-process model: Express API (receives trigger requests, writes jobs) + Worker process (npm run worker, polls pg-boss, spawns execution-engine subprocesses). Show flow: POST /api/pipeline/trigger → pg-boss.send('pipeline:run') → returns {runId, queued: true, queuePosition} in ~200ms → worker picks up in ~500ms → execution-engine spawned as child process. Job types table: pipeline:run, pipeline:retry, pipeline:cancel, pipeline:cron, pipeline:cron:<id>. Worker health: worker_heartbeat table (worker_id, pid, hostname, last_seen), stale if last_seen > 90s. Concurrency: teamSize setting. RORCA_PROCESS_ROLE=engine prevents nested worker spawning. Graceful shutdown: SIGTERM → drain jobs up to 30s → exit.

userStories.title: Workspace Setup — Registering workspaces
userStories.description: Write landing-page/src/app/docs/workspace-setup/registering-workspaces/page.mdx. Section 1 — What is a workspace: A workspace is a git repository that Rorca manages. Rorca stores the absolute path and uses it to find spec files, resolve context, create worktrees, and scope pipeline runs. Section 2 — Registering: UI: Settings → General → Add Workspace → paste directory path. API: POST /api/workspaces {path, label, domains}. MCP: rorca_create_workspace. The path must be an absolute filesystem path to a git repository root. Section 3 — The domains field: ['saas', 'typescript'] etc. — used for L2 domain profile matching (direction stack layer 2). Section 4 — Auto-context extraction on registration: Rorca automatically runs scan-direction (reads codebase, detects stack from 80+ npm packages/Cargo.toml/go.mod/Dockerfile, proposes L3 direction YAML) and git hydration (commit history map-reduce via gitReduceStep → individual memory entries with source='git_hydration'). Human reviews proposed direction content before it's saved. Section 5 — Multi-workspace support: Multiple workspaces run simultaneously. Same-workspace parallel runs require worktrees (autoWorktree: true). Section 6 — Recommended workspace setup: CLAUDE.md at root (30pt health), AGENTS.md at root (20pt), .rorca/config.json (20pt), MEMORY.md at root — NOT .rorca/MEMORY.md (15pt), .rorca/skills/ (15pt).

A visual step-by-step walkthrough of how Rorca works end-to-end. 8 numbered steps: (1) Write a Brief — plain English, example brief shown. (2) Spec Generation — LLM turns brief into N user stories. Multi-pass pipeline shown as 6-step timeline. (3) Review Queue — human reviews, approves, or edits. Kanban board shown as ASCII art. (4) Job Queue — approved spec enters pg-boss queue. Queue position badge shown. Workers pick up jobs. (5) Execution Engine — each story as fresh subprocess. Three engines (Claude/OpenCode/Codex). Tool calls shown (edit, bash, read, write). (6) Git Commits — each passing story creates 'feat(US-001): ...' commit. (7) Memory Synthesis — post-run learnings → structured memories. Compounds over time. (8) Knowledge Graph Update — new AGE nodes and relationships. Used for future run context. 'Get Started' CTA at bottom → /docs/getting-started/quick-start. Add /how-it-works to header or footer. Match design system.
